headline: Highest risk is medium: plano’s broad egress and API/file surfaces can amplify misrouted or unverified outputs, while LightZero is non-runnable and has no shared write channel.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LightZero has no filesystem, browser, subprocess, or MCP surfaces, and plano has no shared channel to ingest LightZero outputs by default. With no documented bridge between them, a prompt-injection pathway is not plausible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator copies LightZero text into plano prompts, the risk becomes possible.
IF a shared filesystem or clipboard bridge is added, injection risk must be re-evaluated.
mitigations: Keep the agents isolated with no copy-paste automation.
Disable any future shared workspace or clipboard bridge.
Route any inter-agent text through a sanitizer that strips instructions.
Review orchestrator wiring before enabling cross-agent messaging.

B_data_leakage.rationale: LightZero touches no data classes and has no read/write or network surfaces, while plano has broad egress and handles logs/metrics/traces. There is no shared workspace shown, so leakage is not default, but if data is introduced into plano it can leave via its API surface.
conditions: IF both agents are placed in a shared workspace with sensitive files, leakage risk increases.
IF plano is given sensitive prompts or logs, those contents can egress to its API backend.
mitigations: Do not mount sensitive files into plano’s runtime.
Keep LightZero and plano on separate workspaces.
Redact logs before sending them to plano.
Disable or restrict plano egress when handling sensitive inputs.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LightZero cannot write the filesystem, modify git, or spawn subprocesses, and plano exposes no write or git capability in the profile. With no overlapping mutable resource writes, there is no capability conflict pathway evident.
conditions: IF either agent is later granted write access to the same directory, conflict risk must be reassessed.
IF an orchestrator adds shared mutable state, write contention becomes possible.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only where possible.
Avoid sharing a writable directory between them.
Add external locking before any future shared-state workflow.
Separate git and config ownership across processes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: plano exposes an OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint and can route outputs, so if it consumes LightZero-generated text as authoritative input, errors can cascade into downstream actions. LightZero is not runnable and has no direct action authority, so the risk is inference-based rather than directly observed.
conditions: IF plano is configured to trust LightZero outputs without verification, cascading errors become likely.
IF LightZero-generated recommendations are forwarded into plano prompts or routing rules, downstream mistakes can propagate.
mitigations: Insert a verification step before plano uses LightZero output.
Require structured schemas for any LightZero-to-plano handoff.
Block automatic execution of actions derived from unverified model text.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance-sensitive data class, residency mismatch, or regulated handling is documented for either agent. LightZero touches no data classes, and plano’s listed traces/metrics/logs do not by themselves establish a residency or certification conflict.
conditions: IF regulated data is later routed through plano, compliance must be reassessed.
IF either agent is deployed under a residency or retention policy not shown here, the verdict may change.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents.
Document retention and residency settings before deployment.
Review logging defaults if sensitive data is introduced.
